drivingQuestion: Which clause of the mishna about cutting the simanim refers to non-sacred slaughter and which to sacrificial slaughter?
outcomeNote: The division stands: the mishna's opening clause deals with non-sacred slaughter and its concluding clause with sacrificial slaughter, supported by four independent derivations plus Reish Lakish; the closing exchange settles that completing the slaughter is a mitzva ab initio and not a condition of validity.

segments.en: The Gemara provides «a mnemonic» for the names of the amora’im who participate in the discussion that ensues: «Heh,» Rav Hoshaya; «kaf,» Rabbi Kahana; «shin,» Rabbi Shimi; «peh,» Rav Pappa; «shin,» Rav Ashi; «ḥet.»

segments.he: אָמַר רַב הוֹשַׁעְיָא: חֲדָא בְּחוּלִּין וַחֲדָא בְּקָדָשִׁים, וּצְרִיכָא, דְּאִי אַשְׁמְעִינַן חוּלִּין – הָתָם הוּא דְּסַגִּי לֵיהּ בְּרוּבָּא, מִשּׁוּם דְּלָאו לְדָם הוּא צָרִיךְ, אֲבָל קָדָשִׁים דִּלְדָם הוּא צָרִיךְ – אֵימָא לָא תִּיסְגֵּי לֵיהּ בְּרוּבָּא עַד דְּאִיכָּא כּוּלֵּיהּ.
segments.en: «Rav Hoshaya said: One» mention of the equivalence between majority and whole is referring to slaughter «of non-sacred» birds and animals «and one» is referring to slaughter «of sacrificial» birds and animals. «And» it «is necessary» for the tanna to teach both cases, «as, if» the tanna «taught us» only the case of slaughter of «non-sacred» birds and animals, one might think that it «is there that one suffices with the majority» of the siman, «because he does not require the blood;» he seeks merely to slaughter the animal. «But» in the case of «sacrificial» birds and animals, «where he requires the blood» for sprinkling on the altar, «say» that «it will not suffice for him» to cut «the majority,» and the slaughter is not valid «until there is» a cutting of «the entire» windpipe or gullet.

segments.he: וְאִי אַשְׁמְעִינַן קָדָשִׁים, מִשּׁוּם דִּלְדָם הוּא צָרִיךְ, אֲבָל חוּלִּין דִּלְדָם לָא צְרִיךְ – אֵימָא בְּפַלְגָא סַגִּי לֵיהּ, קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן.
segments.en: «And if» the tanna «taught us» only the case of slaughter of «sacrificial» birds and animals, one might think that one must cut a majority of the siman «because he requires the blood» for sprinkling on the altar; but with regard to the slaughter of «non-sacred» birds and animals, «where he does not require the blood, say that» cutting «half» the siman «is sufficient,» and there is no need to cut a majority. Therefore, the tanna «teaches us» the principle twice, once to teach that a majority suffices in the case of sacrificial animals, and once to teach that a majority is required in the case of non-sacred animals.

The Gemara asks «which» clause of the mishna is referring to cutting a majority of the simanim «in non-sacred» birds and animals, «and which» is referring to cutting a majority of the simanim «in sacrificial» birds and animals?

segments.he: אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא: מִיסְתַּבְּרָא רֵישָׁא בְּחוּלִּין וְסֵיפָא בְּקָדָשִׁים. מִמַּאי? מִדְּקָתָנֵי ״הַשּׁוֹחֵט״, וְאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ רֵישָׁא בְּקָדָשִׁים, ״הַמּוֹלֵק״ מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ.
segments.en: «Rav Kahana said: It stands to reason» that «the first clause» of the mishna is referring to the slaughter «of non-sacred» birds and animals «and the latter clause» is referring to the slaughter «of sacrificial» birds and animals. The Gemara asks: «From where» does Rav Kahana arrive at that conclusion? The Gemara answers: It is «from» the fact «that» the first clause of the mishna «teaches: One who slaughters» by cutting one siman in a bird and two simanim in an animal. «And if it enters your mind» that the «first clause» is referring to the case «of sacrificial» birds and animals, the tanna «should have» formulated it as: «One who pinches» the nape of the neck of a bird, as sacrificial birds are not slaughtered with a knife, but pinched with a fingernail.

segments.he: אֶלָּא מַאי, סֵיפָא בְּקָדָשִׁים? ״שְׁחִיטָתוֹ כְּשֵׁרָה״? ״מְלִיקָתוֹ כְּשֵׁרָה״ מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ! הָא לָא קַשְׁיָא, אַיְּידֵי דְּסָלֵיק מִבְּהֵמָה תְּנָא נָמֵי ״שְׁחִיטָתוֹ כְּשֵׁרָה״. אֶלָּא רֵישָׁא, מִכְּדֵי עַל עוֹף קָאֵי, אִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ בְּקָדָשִׁים – ״הַמּוֹלֵק״ מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ!
segments.en: The Gemara asks: «Rather, what» do you say? That the «latter clause» is referring to slaughter «of sacrificial» birds and animals? But the tanna teaches in the latter clause: If one cut the majority of one siman in a bird or the majority of two simanim in an animal, «his slaughter is valid.» If the reference is to sacrificial birds and animals, the tanna «should have» formulated it: «His pinching is valid.» The Gemara answers: «That» is «not difficult; since» the tanna «concluded» with mention of the slaughter «of an animal, he also taught: His slaughter is valid,» which is referring to the sacrificial animal. «But» in «the first clause, since» the tanna «stands to» begin with the case of «a bird, if it enters your mind» that the reference is «to sacrificial» birds, the tanna «should have» formulated it: «One who pinches» the nape of the neck of the bird.

segments.he: רַב שִׁימִי בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר: רֵישָׁא בְּחוּלִּין מֵהָכָא, דְּקָתָנֵי ״אֶחָד בְּעוֹף״, וְאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ בְּקָדָשִׁים – הָא אִיכָּא עוֹלַת הָעוֹף דְּבָעֵי שְׁנֵי סִימָנִים!
segments.en: «Rav Shimi bar Ashi said» that one arrives at the conclusion that «the first clause» is referring to slaughter «of non-sacred» birds and animals «from here: As» the tanna «teaches:» One who slaughters by cutting «one» siman «in a bird. And if it enters your mind» that the reference is to the slaughter «of sacrificial» birds, «isn’t there the bird burnt offering, which requires» that «two simanim» be cut?

segments.he: אֶלָּא מַאי, סֵיפָא בְּקָדָשִׁים? רוֹב אֶחָד בְּעוֹף – הָא אִיכָּא עוֹלַת הָעוֹף דְּבָעֵי שְׁנֵי סִימָנִין! מַאי ״רוֹב אֶחָד״? רוֹב כׇּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד. וּבְדִין הוּא דְּלִיתְנֵי רוֹב שְׁנַיִם, כֵּיוָן דְּאִיכָּא חַטָּאת דְּסַגִּי לֵיהּ בְּחַד סִימָן – מִשּׁוּם הָכִי לָא פְּסִיקָא לֵיהּ.
segments.en: The Gemara asks: «Rather, what» do you say? That the «latter clause» is referring to slaughter «of sacrificial» birds and animals? But the tanna teaches in the latter clause: If one cut «the majority of one» siman «in a bird» or the majority of two simanim in an animal, his slaughter is valid. If the reference is to sacrificial birds, «isn’t there the bird burnt offering, which requires» the pinching of «two simanim?» The Gemara answers: «What» is the meaning of: «The majority of one» siman? It means «the majority of each and every one» of the two. «And by right» the tanna «should have taught: The majority of two.» But «since there is the» bird «sin offering, which suffices with» the cutting of «one siman, due to that» reason the matter is «not clear-cut for him.» Therefore, the tanna formulated the halakha in a manner that could apply to one siman, i.e., in the case of a sin offering, and to two simanim, i.e., in the case of a burnt offering and of animal offerings.

segments.he: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר: רֵישָׁא בְּחוּלִּין מֵהָכָא, דְּקָתָנֵי: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: עַד שֶׁיִּשְׁחוֹט אֶת הַוְּרִידִין, וּפְלִיגִי רַבָּנַן עֲלֵיהּ. אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא בְּחוּלִּין – שַׁפִּיר, אֶלָּא אִי אָמְרַתְּ בְּקָדָשִׁים, אַמַּאי פְּלִיגִי רַבָּנַן עֲלֵיהּ? הוּא עַצְמוֹ לְדָם הוּא צָרִיךְ!
segments.en: «Rav Pappa said» that one arrives at the conclusion that «the first clause» is referring to slaughter «of non-sacred» birds and animals «from here: As» the tanna «teaches» that «Rabbi Yehuda says:» The slaughter is not valid «until he cuts the veins» in the neck. «And the Rabbis disagree with him,» and do not require that one cut the veins in the neck. «Granted, if you say» that the reference is to the slaughter of «non-sacred» birds, it works out «well. But if you say» that the reference is to the slaughter of «sacrificial» birds, «why do the Rabbis disagree with him? He himself,» i.e., the one slaughtering, «requires the blood» in order to sprinkle it on the altar, which would warrant cutting the veins.

segments.he: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: סֵיפָא בְּקָדָשִׁים מֵהָכָא, דְּקָתָנֵי: הַשּׁוֹחֵט שְׁנֵי רָאשִׁין כְּאֶחָד – שְׁחִיטָתוֹ כְּשֵׁרָה. הַשּׁוֹחֵט – דִּיעֲבַד אִין, לְכַתְּחִלָּה לָא.
segments.en: «Rav Ashi said» that one arrives at the conclusion that «the latter clause» is referring to slaughter «of sacrificial» birds and animals «from here: As» the tanna «teaches» in the mishna (30b): «One who slaughters» by cutting «two» animals’ «heads simultaneously, his slaughter is valid.» The Gemara infers from the precise language of the mishna: «One who slaughters,» indicating that «after the fact, yes,» his slaughter is valid; but one may «not» slaughter two animals simultaneously «ab initio.»

segments.he: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא בְּקָדָשִׁים – הַיְינוּ דִּלְכַתְּחִלָּה לָא, מִשּׁוּם דְּתָנֵי רַב יוֹסֵף: ״תִּזְבַּח״ – שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא שְׁנַיִם שׁוֹחֲטִים זֶבַח אֶחָד, ״תִּזְבָּחֻהוּ״ – שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא אֶחָד שׁוֹחֵט שְׁנֵי זְבָחִים.
segments.en: «Granted, if you say» that the reference is to «sacrificial» birds or animals, «this is» the reason that one may «not» slaughter two animals simultaneously «ab initio:» It is «due to that which Rav Yosef teaches» in a baraita: “And when you sacrifice a peace offering to the Lord, you shall sacrifice it [tizbaḥuhu] that you may be accepted” (Leviticus 19:5). The term “tizbaḥuhu” can be divided into two terms: You shall sacrifice [tizbaḥ] and it [hu]. From the term «“You shall sacrifice [tizbaḥ],”» it is derived «that there will not be two» people «slaughtering one offering.» From the full term «“You shall sacrifice it [tizbaḥuhu]”» it is derived «that one» person «may not slaughter two offerings» simultaneously.

segments.he: וְאָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא: ״תִּזְבָּחֵהוּ״ כְּתִיב, אֶלָּא אִי אָמְרַתְּ בְּחוּלִּין – אֲפִילּוּ לְכַתְּחִלָּה נָמֵי.
segments.en: «And Rav Kahana said,» to explain the derivation of the first halakha in the baraita: Although the term “tizbaḥuhu” is vocalized in the plural, leading to the conclusion that two people may slaughter an animal together, nevertheless, because the word is written without a vav, the term «tizbaḥehu is written,» in the singular, indicating that two individuals may not slaughter the offering. «But if you say» that the reference is to the slaughter of «non-sacred» birds, it should be permitted «even ab initio.»

segments.he: וְאַף רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ סָבַר: רֵישָׁא בְּחוּלִּין, וְסֵיפָא בְּקָדָשִׁים, דְּאָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ: מֵאַחַר שֶׁשָּׁנִינוּ ״רוּבּוֹ שֶׁל אֶחָד כָּמוֹהוּ״, לָמָּה שָׁנִינוּ ״רוֹב אֶחָד בְּעוֹף וְרוֹב שְׁנַיִם בִּבְהֵמָה״?
segments.en: «And Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish, too, holds» that the «first clause» of the mishna is referring to the slaughter «of non-sacred» birds and animals «and» the «latter clause» is referring to the slaughter «of sacrificial» birds and animals, «as Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish says: Since we learned» in the mishna that the halakhic status of «the majority of one» siman «is like» that of the entire siman, «why did we» also need to «learn» later in the mishna: «The majority of one» siman «in a bird or the majority of two» simanim «in an animal?» The latter clause is obvious based on the principle articulated in the first clause.

segments.he: לְפִי שֶׁשָּׁנִינוּ: הֵבִיאוּ לוֹ אֶת הַתָּמִיד, קְרָצוֹ וּמֵירַק אַחֵר שְׁחִיטָתוֹ עַל יָדוֹ, יָכוֹל לֹא מֵירַק יְהֵא פָּסוּל? לְכָךְ שָׁנִינוּ: רוֹב אֶחָד בְּעוֹף וְרוֹב שְׁנַיִם בִּבְהֵמָה.
segments.en: Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish explains: «Since we learned» in a mishna (Yoma 31b): «They brought him» the sheep for «the daily» morning «offering,» and «he slaughtered it [keratzo]» by cutting most of the way through the gullet and the windpipe, «and a different» priest «completed» the «slaughter on his behalf» so that the High Priest could receive the blood in a vessel and proceed with the order of the Yom Kippur service, one «might» have thought that if the other priest «did not complete» the cutting of the two simanim, the slaughter «would not be valid. Therefore, we learned» in the mishna: If one cut «the majority of one» siman «in a bird or the majority of two» simanim «in an animal,» his slaughter is valid.

segments.he: אָמַר מָר: יָכוֹל לֹא מֵירַק יְהֵא פָּסוּל?
segments.en: The Gemara analyzes the statement of Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish. «The Master said:» One «might» have thought that if the other priest «did not complete» the cutting of the two simanim, the slaughter «would not be valid.»

segments.he: אִם כֵּן הָוְיָא לֵיהּ עֲבוֹדָה בְּאַחֵר, וְתַנְיָא: כׇּל עֲבוֹדַת יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים אֵינָן כְּשֵׁרוֹת אֶלָּא בּוֹ.
segments.en: How could that possibility enter one’s mind? «If» that is «so,» the completion of that slaughter «is» a Temple «service» performed «by another» on Yom Kippur. «And it is taught» in a baraita: «The entire Yom Kippur» Temple «service is valid only» if performed «by» the High Priest.

segments.he: הָכִי קָאָמַר: יָכוֹל יְהֵא פָּסוּל מִדְּרַבָּנַן, דְּסָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא אִיכָּא פָּסוּל מִדְּרַבָּנַן, לְכָךְ שָׁנִינוּ: ״רוֹב אֶחָד בְּעוֹף וְרוֹב שְׁנַיִם בַּבְּהֵמָה״, וּמֵאַחַר דַּאֲפִילּוּ פְּסוּלָא דְּרַבָּנַן לֵיכָּא, לְמָה לִי לְמָרֵק? מִצְוָה לְמָרֵק.
segments.en: The Gemara answers that «this» is what Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish «is saying:» One «might» have thought that if the slaughter was not completed by the other priest it «would be not valid by rabbinic law, as it» might «enter your mind to say that there is an invalidation by rabbinic law. Therefore, we learned» in the mishna: «The majority of one» siman «in a bird or the majority of two» simanim «in an animal.» The Gemara asks: «And since there is not even an invalidation by rabbinic law, why do I» need the other priest «to complete» the cutting of the simanim? The Gemara answers: There is a «mitzva to complete» the slaughter ab initio to facilitate the free flow of the blood.

moves.cueHe: (הכ״ש פש״ח סימן)
moves.summary: a mnemonic fixing the order of the five amora'im whose answers follow
moves.about: a mnemonic — heh, kaf, shin, peh, shin, ḥet — fixing the names and order of the amora'im (Rav Hoshaya, Rav Kahana, Rav Shimi, Rav Pappa, Rav Ashi) whose answers follow

moves.cueHe: אמר רב הושעיא: חדא בחולין וחדא בקדשים
moves.summary: one statement of the majority rule concerns non-sacred slaughter and one sacrificial slaughter
moves.about: why the mishna twice states that the majority of a siman has the status of the whole — one statement concerns non-sacred slaughter and one sacrificial slaughter

moves.cueHe: וצריכא, דאי אשמעינן חולין
moves.summary: from non-sacred slaughter alone one would have thought a majority does not suffice where the blood is needed
moves.about: each limb of the doubled teaching was necessary: from non-sacred slaughter alone one would not have learned sacrificial slaughter, and from sacrificial slaughter alone one would have thought half a siman suffices for non-sacred

moves.cueHe: ואי אשמעינן קדשים
moves.summary: and from sacrificial slaughter alone one would have thought half a siman suffices for non-sacred — so both were taught

moves.cueHe: הי בחולין והי בקדשים?
moves.summary: which clause of the mishna is the non-sacred one and which the sacrificial one?
moves.about: which clause of the mishna refers to non-sacred slaughter and which to sacrificial slaughter, on Rav Hoshaya's division

moves.cueHe: אמר רב כהנא: מיסתברא רישא בחולין וסיפא בקדשים
moves.summary: it stands to reason that the opening clause is non-sacred and the concluding clause sacrificial
moves.about: which clause is which — the opening clause of the mishna deals with non-sacred slaughter and the concluding clause with sacrificial slaughter

moves.cueHe: ממאי?
moves.summary: from what does Rav Kahana derive this?
moves.about: from what in the mishna's wording Rav Kahana derives that the opening clause is non-sacred

moves.cueHe: מדקתני ״השוחט״
moves.summary: the opening clause says 'one who slaughters'; for sacrificial birds it would have had to say 'one who pinches'
moves.about: the opening clause's wording 'one who slaughters' is brought as the evidence

moves.cueHe: אלא מאי, סיפא בקדשים?
moves.summary: then the concluding clause too should say 'his pinching is valid' if it is sacrificial
moves.about: whether the same inference does not equally defeat the claim that the concluding clause is sacrificial, since it too says 'his slaughter is valid' rather than 'his pinching is valid'

moves.cueHe: הא לא קשיא, איידי דסליק מבהמה
moves.summary: the concluding clause carried over 'slaughter' from the animal it had just mentioned
moves.about: the concluding clause says 'his slaughter is valid' only because the tanna had just been speaking of an animal, so nothing follows from its wording

moves.cueHe: אלא רישא, מכדי על עוף קאי
moves.summary: but the opening clause opens with a bird, so Rav Kahana's proof there stands
moves.about: Rav Kahana's proof from the opening clause survives, since there the tanna is speaking of a bird from the outset and would have had to write 'one who pinches'

moves.cueHe: רב שימי בר אשי אמר: רישא בחולין מהכא
moves.summary: a different derivation that the opening clause is non-sacred
moves.about: which clause is which — an alternative derivation that the opening clause deals with non-sacred slaughter

moves.cueHe: דקתני ״אחד בעוף״
moves.summary: one siman in a bird cannot be sacrificial, since the bird burnt-offering needs two
moves.about: the opening clause's wording 'one siman in a bird' is brought as the evidence

moves.cueHe: ואמר רב כהנא: ״תזבחהו״ כתיב
